title: Cancellation by Tidemark: Notice Requirements for HomeFlood Policies
content:
**Grounds.** Tidemark cancels a HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies policy mid-term only for nonpayment (NONPAYMENT) of a past-due installment, or for material misrepresentation in the application. It does so only by a written notice mailed to the insured and to the mortgagee of record.

**Notice periods.** Each period runs in calendar days from the mailing date to the cancellation date stated on the notice.

| Ground | Notice period |
|---|---|
| nonpayment | the tier's nonpayment notice period |
| material misrepresentation | the tier's insurer cancellation notice period |

**Status.** A notice of cancellation is issued only on a policy whose status is active, as the policy record shows, and it moves the policy to pending cancellation.

**Notice runs out uncured.** The policy is cancelled on the stated date. The unearned share of the net term premium after that date is credited pro rata by days, with no paid-claim bar. The credit is set against any earned premium still owed, and only a remaining credit balance is refunded to the payor of record.

*Hypothetical illustration:* a nonpayment notice mailed on 2 May on a HomeFlood Renters policy states a cancellation date 10 days later, 12 May. The same notice on a HomeFlood Estate policy states a date 45 days later, 16 June.

The tier figures this rule reads (its nonpayment notice period and its insurer cancellation notice period) are those of the tier's own schedule.
